judgments.marker: Google sign-in phish: exclude command keys from credential paths
Python PTY reverse shell: relocate and consolidate connect traits
Assessment-shaped reverse shell: preserve active-chain detection

behavior: JavaScript-compatible TypeScript injects synthetic browser chrome with a Google login URL, captures successive plaintext passwords and an OTP, emits the account record on Socket.IO, and dispatches remotely received MFA retry and completion commands. Reserved .invalid endpoint prevents successful public-network delivery as shipped; it does not make the credential phishing logic legitimate.

Python module connects an outbound socket, duplicates the connected descriptor onto 0/1/2 in a loop, and starts /bin/sh through pty.spawn. The literal IP is a documentation address; static evidence establishes the reverse-shell chain, not successful contact.

Python has the same active module-scope chain following an assessment-style class declaration. HTTPClient and OptIP are undefined in the isolated file, so standalone execution raises before the chain unless a host supplies those names. No callable check or payload generator contains the chain; plugin metadata is not a benign execution guard.
identity: Generic phishing frontend and PTY reverse-shell sources; no supported family, package, actor or real endpoint attribution.
changes: Exclude ambiguous bare slash-prefixed password/credential words from the filesystem path atom. Positive qualified paths and negative command-map keys are stored in testdata/taxonomy/credential-command-path.

Move python-connect-ip-port from socket/dial to socket/connect, retaining matcher, criticality, confidence and scope. Update all three exact consumers. Preserve legacy dial selector coverage by including the relocated atom in existing python-dial alternatives. Other dial rules retain their existing identities pending broader migration.

Consolidate socket-connect-method-short and socket-connect-method-named into their existing canonical socket-connect-method. Only their canonical composite referenced either removed atom. Use structured call records to stop comment/string matches; retain canonical exclusions. This also keeps connect below its directory review limit. Broader connect consumers retain the supported socket-like call claim.

validation.controls: Qualified credential paths match; command keys do not. Actual Python connect calls match; prose does not. Hostile authoring precision checked with test-rules.
validation.inspection: Read full source and cleave facts including symbols and flow; no obfuscation or embedded payload. Rizin inspection is not useful for these source files; binwalk is not installed.
